items.note: Orders and u2 used Parkland 4 mL/kg/%TBSA (11,520 mL) and keyed a 'catch-up' rate of 823 mL/hour, which is older teaching and a debated point. Order now reads ABLS adult thermal starting estimate 2 mL x kg x %TBSA, half in first 8 h from injury, titrated hourly to UOP 0.5 mL/kg/h. u2 rewritten: b2 key 5,760 mL (11,520 kept as the Parkland distractor, 2,880 as first-8-h share); b3 replaced the debated catch-up rate with 'half counted from the time of injury' (vs arrival / IV start). Rationale rewritten (fluid creep, titration to ~40 mL/h). Stem/blank wording no longer says Parkland. Refs -> aba-abls, openstax-medsurg. Other items verified (airway priority, IV opioids, Tdap, no prophylactic antibiotics, escharotomy cue, order sequence O2 -> IV/LR -> catheter -> wound care).

Content verified against ACOG severe-feature criteria (BP >=160/110 confirmed within 15 min, refractory headache, visual changes, RUQ/epigastric pain; platelets 136k, normal LFTs/creatinine not severe), Mg toxicity actions and BP goal. Refs changed to acog-preeclampsia, openstax-maternal, ismp-highalert (dropped dailymed).

Refs -> aap-neonatal-glucose, openstax-maternal. g5 keyed option was much the longest (giveaway) and implied a syringe pump is required; shortened to 'Give 8.9 mL of D10W IV as prescribed, then start the infusion' and adjusted the rationale. d3 rationale said 'BUN and creatinine are already rising' but there is no baseline and creatinine 0.5 is near normal; changed to 'the BUN is already elevated'. Verified 9% weight loss, compensated shock, 20 mL/kg = 220 mL, no KCl until voiding, order sequence.
